Roast Turkey

Served at: Christmas Day · Thanksgiving Day (United States)

Serves 8-12Prep 30 min (plus thawing time if frozen)Cook 3-4 hours

Roast Turkey is the quintessential centerpiece of both Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day feasts in the United States, symbolizing abundance, family gathering, and gratitude. This impressive dish, often surrounded by an array of seasonal side dishes, brings warmth and tradition to holiday tables, creating cherished memories for generations.

Ingredients

  • 1 (12-14 lb) whole turkey, thawed if frozen
  • 1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 large yellow onion, quartered
  • 2 celery stalks, roughly chopped
  • 2 carrots, roughly chopped
  • 4 sprigs fresh rosemary
  • 6 sprigs fresh thyme
  • 1 head garlic, cut in half horizontally
  • 1 tablespoon (15g) salt
  • 1 teaspoon (5g) black pepper
  • 2 cups (470ml) chicken or vegetable broth

Method

  1. Thaw the turkey: If frozen, ensure the turkey is fully thawed in the refrigerator (allow approximately 24 hours for every 4-5 pounds).
  2. Preheat oven: Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C). Remove the giblets and neck from the turkey cavities and discard or save for gravy. Pat the turkey thoroughly dry with paper towels, inside and out.
  3. Prepare the turkey: Place the turkey in a large roasting pan. In a small bowl, mix the softened butter with salt and pepper. Rub the butter mixture all over the turkey, including under the skin of the breast if desired.
  4. Stuff the cavity: Place the quartered onion, chopped celery, chopped carrots, rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs, and garlic halves into the turkey cavity.
  5. Truss (optional) and add liquid: If desired, truss the turkey legs together with kitchen twine. Pour the chicken or vegetable broth into the bottom of the roasting pan.
  6. Roast the turkey: Place the turkey in the preheated oven. Roast for 3 to 4 hours, or until a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh (without touching bone) reads 165°F (74°C).
  7. Baste and brown: Baste the turkey every 30-45 minutes with the pan juices. If the skin is browning too quickly, loosely tent the turkey with aluminum foil.
  8. Rest the turkey: Once cooked, remove the turkey from the oven, transfer it to a large cutting board, and tent loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in a more tender and flavorful bird.
  9. Carve and serve: Carve the turkey and arrange on a platter. Serve warm with pan drippings or gravy.

Tips

  • For extra crispy skin, increase the oven temperature to 400°F (200°C) for the last 20-30 minutes of roasting.
  • Consider brining the turkey overnight for an exceptionally moist and flavorful result.
  • Save the pan drippings to make a delicious homemade gravy.
